idiom_name: ||= memoization and Hash#default_proc locally; ActiveSupport::Cache stores for TTL
implementation_notes: Ruby's idiomatic cache is memoization: an instance variable populated with @value ||= compute, or a Hash with h[k] ||= compute, replaces the classic structure for per-instance reuse, and Hash#default_proc gives computed defaults with the same shape. Neither Hash nor the memo idiom provides eviction or TTL, so bounded or expiring caches need a policy you write or a store library - ActiveSupport::Cache::MemoryStore/RedisCache with expires_in and Rails.cache.fetch is the framework answer in Rails. ObjectSpace::WeakMap and weak references let object-keyed caches follow the GC instead of pinning keys, which the default Hash cannot do. Hand-rolled Hash memoization is for local, bounded reuse; anything shared across processes belongs in a cache store.
pitfalls: ||= cannot memoize false or nil results - it recomputes them on every call; use defined?(@x) ? @x : (@x = compute) for those.
A memoizing Hash holds strong references to its keys: caches keyed by domain objects pin them forever; ObjectSpace::WeakMap or weak references are the GC-friendly alternative.
Hash memoization is only accidentally thread-safe under MRI's GVL; JRuby, TruffleRuby and Ractor-based code can interleave, so shared caches need a mutex or a store with atomic fetch.
Instance-variable memoization is invisible to callers and survives test cases inside long-lived objects - expose a reset path and test it.
